questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Antigua and Barbuda?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the Antigua and Barbuda article.

questions.proof: English is the official language, but many of the locals speak Antiguan Creole.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Christopher Columbus was the first European to see Antigua in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the fifteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “European arrival and slavery” part of the Antigua and Barbuda article.

questions.proof: Christopher Columbus was the first European to see Antigua in 1493.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “A major revolt was planned in _____, led by Prince Klaas, but it was discovered early and the leaders were executed.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the eighteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Antigua and Barbuda article, under the heading “Colonial era”.

questions.proof: A major revolt was planned in 1736, led by Prince Klaas, but it was discovered early and the leaders were executed.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Vere Bird led until _____, followed by his son Lester Bird until 2004.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Antigua and Barbuda article, under the heading “Independence era”.

questions.proof: Vere Bird led until 1994, followed by his son Lester Bird until 2004.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Slaves faced very harsh treatment, which led to revolts in _____ and 1729.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the eighteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Antigua and Barbuda article, under the heading “Colonial era”.

questions.proof: Slaves faced very harsh treatment, which led to revolts in 1701 and 1729.
